extracted.intended_audience: Scholars/authors preparing and submitting manuscripts to the American Journal of Political Science (AJPS)
extracted.subtask_description: Official submission and editorial guidelines for manuscripts to the American Journal of Political Science, covering acceptable submission types (articles, research notes, correspondence), scope and originality requirements, formatting/word limits, ethics/IRB, peer-review process, and appeals policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall contribution standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeks manuscripts that make outstanding contributions to scholarly knowledge about notable theoretical concerns, empirical issues, or methodological strategies in any subfield of political science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts should address an important research problem or question, display a high level of creativity or innovation in research, contribute in a novel way to a body of knowledge, and (as appropriate) demonstrate state-of-the-art use of appropriate methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address an important research problem or question
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts submitted for review should address an important research problem or question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Importance of the problem is a core criterion for selection and is part of the journal's contribution standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity and innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should display a high level of creativity or innovation in research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creativity/innovation may be theoretical, empirical, or methodological and is evaluated alongside contribution to knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novel contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must contribute in a novel way to a body of knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty is required — manuscripts that do not contain original arguments or analyses will not be reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate, state-of-the-art methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should demonstrate state-of-the-art use of appropriate methodology (as appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological rigor and use of appropriate contemporary methods are expected where relevant to the research question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality requirement (no previously published material)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must not contain material that has already been published elsewhere (without appropriate citation or acknowledgment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duplicate publication or reuse of published material without acknowledgement is disqualifying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical rigor and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must be analytically rigorous, of high quality, and self-contained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of rigor, low quality, or dependence on external/unavailable material are reasons for non-review or rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects/IRB approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts reporting studies involving human subjects must have appropriate Institutional Review Board approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to have appropriate IRB approval will prevent review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not simultaneously under review elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts submitted to AJPS must not be simultaneously under review at another journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simultaneous submissions are explicitly prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission type restrictions — no book reviews or essays on current events
rubrics_metrics.description: AJPS does not review book reviews or essays on current events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those genres are outside the scope of the journal's accepted manuscript types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with substantive, stylistic, formatting, and anonymity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must comply with the substantive, stylistic, formatting, and anonymity requirements described by the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply with these requirements is a reason for desk rejection; see the journal's Manuscript Preparation and Submission pages for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: No prior AJPS review
rubrics_metrics.description: AJPS will not review manuscripts that have been reviewed previously at the AJPS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts previously considered by AJPS should not be resubmitted for another full review cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article word limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Article submissions have a 10,000 word limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure full-length article manuscripts do not exceed the stated length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Note word limit and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Note submissions have a 4,000 word limit and will be confined to methodology papers (including methodology papers in normative political theory) and meta-analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research notes must start their title with the words “Research Note,” and essays that primarily present new data or offer replications without significant theoretical or research design innovations will not be accepted as research notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Note title formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of each Research Note will start with the words, “Research Note,” (e.g., “Research Note: Populism and Violence Against Immigrants”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formatting helps distinguish research notes from full-length articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence category — purpose and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence is short critical essays (4,000-word limit) in which scholars who are not the original authors challenge the central claims of a previously published AJPS article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondence should convincingly challenge the central claims of a recently published AJPS manuscript and will be especially considered when providing broader contributions (e.g., new data collection, multiple replications, or methodological insights).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence title formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of each Correspondence piece will follow a standardized format beginning with the word “Correspondence” (e.g., “Correspondence: [Original Article Title], A Reanalysis and Discussion”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardized titling distinguishes correspondence from other submission types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence desk-rejection for minor errors
rubrics_metrics.description: If a correspondence submission simply identifies a relatively minor error in the original manuscript (e.g., mislabeling a variable, misreporting a result, or a coding error), editors might desk reject the Correspondence and invite the original author to submit a Correction or the journal to publish an Erratum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondence should do more than point out minor mistakes; substantial challenges or broader contributions are expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence scope limitation (AJPS articles only)
rubrics_metrics.description: AJPS will not publish Correspondence that addresses articles published in other journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondence is limited to challenging AJPS-published articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections and Errata policy
rubrics_metrics.description: AJPS publishes Corrections—short notes in which authors of original AJPS publications acknowledge errors in their work; Corrections appear under the original authors’ names. An Erratum indicates a publisher error rather than an author error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections are author-initiated acknowledgments of error; Errata are for publisher mistakes (e.g., assembling a result incorrectly in a table).

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-review model — double-blind
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts are selected for publication in the AJPS based on a double-blind review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must follow anonymity requirements; reviewers do not know author identities and editors manage the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation to perform peer review for the journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors and co-authors of submissions to the AJPS are expected to review manuscripts for the Journal when invited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AJPS Co-Editors reserve the right to refuse submissions from authors who repeatedly fail to provide reviews when invited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of reviews and editors’ decision authority
rubrics_metrics.description: All reviews are advisory to the AJPS Co-Editors, who are responsible for publication decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referee recommendations inform but do not determine editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and turnaround expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors are committed to providing constructive and informative manuscript reviews and efficient, timely turnaround, but review speed is directly affected by the timeliness of referee responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should expect the review process may take several months; prompt referee responses help speed the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If authors wish to appeal an editorial decision, they should send their appeal to ajps@ajps.org and must wait at least 24 hours between receiving the editorial decision and sending the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All appeals are judged by the editors-in-chief, who may consult others; the decisions of the editors-in-chief on appeals are final.
